quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 40 Questions • Passing Score 35

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left part
The center part
The right part
The shoulder

questions.correctAnswerText: The left part
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of the lane when passing another vehicle on the left. This helps you see ahead better and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, you should adjust the:

options.text: Brakes.
Seat.
Suspension.
Brake light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the settings recommended for that weight.

questions.question: Eye protection, such as goggles or a face shield, is:

options.text: Recommended.
Required.
Only required for riders under 18.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required.
questions.explanation: Eye protection is required for all riders of any age. You can use goggles, a face shield, glasses, or an approved windshield.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that increases visibility.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, choose a lane position that makes you more visible to other drivers. Cover the clutch and both brakes to reduce your reaction time. Slow down when approaching an intersection. Do not change your speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: This sign warns that:

options.text: There is a steep hill ahead.
No trucks are allowed on an upcoming hill.
A logging road is ahead.
There are trucks on an upcoming hill.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill or downgrade is coming ahead.

questions.question: Which factor does not affect a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
Body weight
How quickly the alcohol was consumed
How often alcohol is consumed

questions.correctAnswerText: How often alcohol is consumed
questions.explanation: Three main factors affect BAC: how much alcohol you drink, how fast you drink it, and your body weight. Your sex, physical condition, and whether you have eaten may also affect BAC.

questions.question: The best lane position for a motorcycle:

options.text: Is in the left part of the lane, next to the centerline.
Is in the right part of the lane, next to the curb.
Can vary depending on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can vary depending on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position at all times. Choose the lane position that gives you the most visibility and space around you. Change your position as traffic conditions change.

questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Meet U.S. DOT standards.
Fit snugly.
Have obvious defects.
Have been worn in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a crash.
questions.explanation: For the best protection, wear a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards, fits snugly, and has no defects. Replace any helmet that was worn during a crash.

questions.question: An engine will seize due to:

options.text: A lack of oil.
A lack of fuel.
Improper tire inflation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lack of oil.
questions.explanation: Engines seize when they run low on oil. Without oil, the engine's moving parts cannot slide smoothly against each other and the engine overheats.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a benefit of riding in a tight group?

options.text: It takes up minimal space on the highway.
The group is easy to see.
The group is unlikely to get separated.
Riders in a tight group reach their destination faster than riders in a spread-out group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders in a tight group reach their destination faster than riders in a spread-out group.
questions.explanation: Riding in a tight group is better than a spread-out group because it takes up less road space, is easier for others to see, and is less likely to get separated at traffic lights and during passes.

questions.question: To see better when you are about to pass a vehicle on its left, you should:

options.text: Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the middle of your lane.
Stand up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride on the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride on the left side of your lane when you are about to pass. This helps you see ahead better and makes oncoming traffic see you better.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Steep hill ahead.
Pedestrian crossing ahead.
Low railroad crossing.
Low clearance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the bridge or overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not go through if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (13 feet 6 inches in this example).

questions.question: This is a __________ sign.

options.text: Stop
Wrong way
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield
questions.explanation: A triangle pointing down means yield. Slow down to a safe speed when you see this sign. Stop if you need to. If you stop, do so at the marked line if there is one.

questions.question: Your front tire is flat if your steering suddenly feels:

options.text: Heavy.
Loose.
Soft.

questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: Heavy steering means your front tire may be flat. Stop right away and check your tires.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is not recommended because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is light colored.
Is not important.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Always wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration in addition to their other safety benefits.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid danger, you should:

options.text: Use only the front brake while swerving.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: If you need to brake and swerve, do these actions one at a time. Never brake while swerving because your motorcycle could fall over.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Not worry about space cushions.
Add more space around yourself.
Use half your normal space cushion.
Keep a safe space around yourself.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe space around yourself.
questions.explanation: Ride close together as a group but always keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: On a wet road, avoid riding in:

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The center of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
Any part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars drips into a strip in the center of the lane. This strip is slippery when wet. You can usually ride to the side of this strip and still be in the center of your lane.

questions.question: When rain starts, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull over and wait for the rain to stop.
Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane becomes very slippery when it first rains. Ride in the tire tracks left by other vehicles. The left tire track is usually the safest choice.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run next to the road, you should:

options.text: Cross at a 90-degree angle.
Never cross the tracks.
Cross at a 45-degree angle or steeper.
Cross very slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross at a 45-degree angle or steeper.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks, trolley tracks, or road seams at an angle of at least 45 degrees. Make a quick, sharp turn. Crossing slowly or at a shallow angle can catch your tires and make you lose balance.

questions.question: What can help if your drive chain slips?

options.text: Tighten the chain
Loosen the chain
Use more throttle
Apply the rear brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Tighten the chain
questions.explanation: If your chain slips, try tightening it. If tightening does not fix the problem, replace the chain before riding again.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn
No left turn
No right turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. Turning right here is unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: The center of the lane often has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it rains
Ride only on the oily strip for better traction
Avoid the entire center of the lane
Do not worry about oil in the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it rains
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks builds up in the lane's center. When the road is dry, this strip usually has enough traction for a motorcycle. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride to either side and still stay in the center of your lane. Avoid it when wet.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Use your high beam
Use headlights from other vehicles to help you see
Make yourself visible
Ride only on the left side of your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only on the left side of your lane
questions.explanation: When riding at night, use your high beam (unless following or meeting another vehicle), use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective clothes. Change your lane position as needed to see, be seen, and maintain safe space around you.

questions.question: When your motorcycle has a sidecar, where should the passenger sit?

options.text: On the motorcycle seat
In the sidecar
Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar
Neither on the motorcycle nor in the sidecar

questions.correctAnswerText: In the sidecar
questions.explanation: Your passenger should ride in the sidecar. They should keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Is not serious
Takes away your ability to change direction
Will fix itself
Is only a problem if the front tire also skids

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes away your ability to change direction
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is very dangerous and can cause a violent crash and serious injury or death. Too much rear brake pressure can lock the rear wheel. When the wheel locks, you cannot change direction. You must release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: The center portion of a traffic lane is where:

options.text: Debris and oil from cars often collect
Motorcycle riders should always travel for safety
Most accidents happen
Drivers are least likely to see a motorcycle

questions.correctAnswerText: Debris and oil from cars often collect
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is where debris and oil from cars collect. Other hazards like utility hole covers are also found in the center of the lane.

questions.question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what should you do?

options.text: Always stop before entering
Yield only to traffic on the right
Yield only to traffic on the left
Slow down and give the right-of-way to other traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give the right-of-way to other traffic
questions.explanation: A yield sign means you must slow down and let other traffic go first before entering the intersection.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, you should:

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake
Brake and swerve at the same time
Choose to either brake or swerve
Do not swerve and only use the front brake

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, one after the other. Do not brake while swerving, as this can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. Tire failure is usually noticed by a change in how your motorcycle handles.

questions.question: When loading cargo onto a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Put lighter items near the front.
Avoid placing items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Put heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle can affect your control.

questions.question: Why should motorcyclists in a group avoid riding in pairs?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections may make it hard for riders to see.
Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to avoid hazards.
It is too hard for riders on the left side to exit a highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: When traveling in a group, do not ride in pairs. Neither rider will have enough room to maneuver to avoid hazards.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT affect blood alcohol content (BAC)?

options.text: The amount of alcohol consumed
How fast the alcohol is consumed
The drinker's body weight
How often the drinker consumes alcohol

questions.correctAnswerText: How often the drinker consumes alcohol
questions.explanation: Three factors affect blood alcohol content: the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it is consumed, and the drinker's body weight. Driving while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do to increase your chances of being seen at an intersection?

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.
Keep your headlight on.
Reduce your space cushion.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on and ride in a position that helps other drivers see you. Maintain a space cushion so you can take action if needed. Do not assume another driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time to a hazard?

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing.
Pull the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians only.
Intersection ahead.
Hiking trails ahead.
School crossing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: School crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a school crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Why should you not change gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: Your motorcycle may stall.
You might go too fast.
Other drivers may not expect you to change gears.
The uneven surface makes shifting gears harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle might stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: What should you do when turning?

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn, not your shoulders.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders can make you steer off course.

questions.question: How does the stopping distance for motorcycles compare to cars?

options.text: Cars need much longer to stop.
Cars need a little longer to stop.
Motorcycles need longer to stop.
Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles and cars take about the same time to stop.
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, motorcycles and cars have nearly the same stopping distance. However, slippery pavement makes quick stops especially difficult for motorcycles.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane.
The center portion of the lane.
The right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, ride in the center of your lane. This is the safest position. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle increases the risk of collision. Riding on the far side may encourage the driver to return to your lane too soon.
